targets.authors: Napier J. N., Jost J. T.
targets.title: Why are conservatives happier than liberals?
targets.evidence_quote: We failed to replicate Napier and Jost’s finding that system-justifying ideology mediated the relationship between conservatism and life satisfaction.
targets.outcome_quote: In a study ( N = 816), we find that conservatives are more satisfied with life than liberals and that conservatism is associated with higher socioeconomic status (SES). Taking SES as a starting point, we find that those with high SES have access to more group memberships and that this is associated with higher life satisfaction. We failed to replicate Napier and Jost’s finding that system-justifying ideology mediated the relationship between conservatism and life satisfaction.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Abstract confirms the conservatism–happiness association but explicitly fails the proposed mediation; no overall verdict about both findings is available. Citation copied from publisher reference listing, with its printed initials retained.
